notes: One of the fastest-growing glacial lakes in the Himalaya; outlet lowered ~3 m by a 2016 Nepal Army works project to reduce risk. Classic potentially dangerous glacial lake (PDGL).
references: ICIMOD/UNDP 2020 PDGL inventory; Bajracharya et al. 2020

notes: Largest glacial lake in Nepal; siphon/gated outlet built 2000 to lower level ~3 m; early-warning system installed downstream.
PDGL feeding the Marsyangdi; large hydropower assets downstream.
Among the highest-priority PDGLs identified in the 2020 inventory; very large volume.
Moraine-dam failure on 4 Aug 1985 destroyed the nearly complete Namche small hydropower plant, bridges and farmland ~90 km downstream. Reference event for Nepal GLOF risk.
PDGL in the Dudh Koshi basin.
High-volume PDGL in the Hongu/Arun system.
PDGL in the Tamor basin, far-eastern Nepal.

Not a classic moraine-dammed lake, but the 26 Aug 2026 ice-rock avalanche briefly dammed the Bhote Koshi then breached, producing a debris flow / flash flood ~100 km downstream. Corridor flagged for cascading cryosphere hazard.
